## Description

**What**: The walking-skeleton slice of the load-bearing verifier gate. Wraps a single per-step validation command (chosen for simplicity, e.g., `lint`) in a thin shim (`commit-step`) that captures full output and writes a result artifact + breadcrumb. A new pre-commit hook reads artifacts and refuses the commit when the expected artifact is missing. Hook is feature-flagged off by default; Story 7 flips the default after skip markers ship.

**Why**: SC1 of the parent epic, walking-skeleton-sized — proves the wrapper-driven artifact verification pattern end-to-end before extending coverage to all steps.

**Scope**:
- IN: One wrapper script (`.claude/scripts/dso commit-step <name>`) that runs the underlying command, captures full stdout+stderr, writes `<name>.result` artifact + breadcrumb in the worktree's artifacts dir; one new pre-commit hook (`pre-commit-compliance-verifier.sh`) that reads `<name>.result` and refuses the commit on absence; hook installation registers via the existing `reinstall-hooks.sh` path.
- OUT: extending wrappers to other steps (Story 3); overlay verification (Story 5); truncation handling (Story 4); skip markers (Story 7); worktree-context safety (Story 6); the override path (Story 1, already shipped).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, running `.claude/scripts/dso commit-step <name>` for the chosen step produces a `<name>.result` artifact + breadcrumb in the worktree's artifacts directory.
  ← Satisfies: "SC1 — wrapper-written validation artifacts"
- When this story is complete, a synthetic test that removes the `<name>.result` artifact triggers the pre-commit hook block.
  ← Satisfies: "SC1 — verifier as load-bearing pre-commit gate (single-step proof)"
- When this story is complete, the new pre-commit hook is installed via `reinstall-hooks.sh` with the executable bit set, and a regression test verifies executable-bit preservation across plugin sync.
  ← Satisfies: gate-must-actually-run guarantee
- When this story is complete, the new pre-commit hook is feature-flagged off by default in `dso-config.conf` (`hooks.compliance_verifier.enabled=false`); Story 7 flips this default once skip markers ship. Test: a fresh project with default config commits cleanly without the verifier blocking.
  ← Satisfies: safe rollout precondition
- When this story is complete, any pre-existing host-project `pre-commit` hook continues to execute alongside the new verifier (chain semantics). Test fixture: install a marker host pre-commit hook, install the plugin's verifier, confirm both run.
  ← Satisfies: consumer impact: existing host hook chains preserved
- When this story is complete, `ARTIFACTS_DIR` resolution works in CI environments without requiring an externally-set env var — derives from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` per `get_artifacts_dir()` semantics.
  ← Satisfies: CI compatibility
- When this story is complete, the hook handles the first-run condition (artifacts directory absent) by passing-with-warning rather than blocking.
  ← Satisfies: bootstrap safety
- When this story is complete, the wrapper handles exit 144 (SIGTERM/~73s ceiling) by writing a `<name>.timeout` artifact (rather than no artifact) so the verifier's diagnostic message names the failure mode.
  ← Satisfies: timeout diagnostic clarity
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic.
  ← Satisfies: TDD Done-of-Done

## Considerations

- [Reliability] First-run absent artifacts dir; executable-bit preservation; host-hook chain preservation; CI env compat; exit-144 handling — all surfaced as separate done definitions above.
- [Maintainability] Breadcrumb log format includes observability-compatible fields (timestamp, step name, agent context, optional cost hooks) so `5df7-63ac` integrated observability can consume the same log.
- [Security] Hook reads only from `$ARTIFACTS_DIR` for the worktree where the hook runs — does not span worktrees in this story (Story 6 adds full worktree-context safety).

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
